definition: Software that automatically displays or downloads advertisements on a user's device, often without their explicit consent, to generate revenue for the software creator.
metaDescription: Learn about adware - unwanted software that displays ads on your device. Understand how it works, privacy risks, and protection methods.
simpleExplanation: Adware is like having someone sneak billboards into your house without permission. It's software that shows you ads you didn't ask for, often slowing down your computer and tracking what you do online to show more targeted advertisements.
whyItMatters: Adware violates your privacy by tracking browsing habits, degrades device performance, creates security vulnerabilities, and exposes you to potentially malicious content. It can also lead to unwanted purchases or identity theft.
technicalDetail: Adware typically installs through software bundles, browser extensions, or drive-by downloads. It modifies browser settings, injects ads into web pages, redirects searches, and often communicates with remote servers to download new ad content and report user behavior data.

examples.explanation: You download a free photo editor that secretly installs adware, causing pop-up ads to appear constantly while browsing, even when the photo editor isn't running.
Adware changes your browser's homepage to a search engine filled with ads and redirects your searches to advertising-heavy websites you didn't intend to visit.
A mobile app displays excessive, intrusive ads that cover content, track your location and app usage, and drain your battery faster than normal.
